beats.headline: Named in a drunken confession
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut, under the Buzzed debuff from a blended corpse, informs Crawler Carl that she loves him. Almost as much as Bea. Almost as much as Ferdinand. Ferdinand is the other cat. That is the whole entry: a cat, ranked above the man who carried her down the stairs, by a cat. I keep records on everything in this dungeon. This one I opened for the ranking.

beats.headline: His name was Gravy Boat
beats.text: A caller on Danger Zone asks Princess Donut who Ferdinand is. The answer given is the love of her life: a star-crossed ruffian, branded a Moggie, hunted by the authorities, who called to her from outside the window. Carl identifies him as the creepy yellow cat that came to the window when she was in heat. His name was Gravy Boat, and he belonged to Marjory on the first floor. Animal control never managed to catch him. "He preferred Ferdinand," says Donut.

beats.headline: Gravy Boat
beats.text: Subject is on Earth. His real name is Gravy Boat. He is Beatrice's neighbour's cat, who used to yowl at her window when Princess was in heat; she called him Ferdinand to shoo him off. She found him in a tree beside the hole where her building was, skin and bones. He is also an A-tier target on the season's Walk-On list, and two bounty hunters have scanned six cats in the area looking for him. Odette's orders: a bounty cube, and a delivery to Borant.

beats.headline: Familiar to Queen Imogen
beats.text: Update to the file. The party runs into the High Elves. The High Elves have a queen, Queen Imogen, and the queen has a familiar, and the familiar is Ferdinand. Yes. That Ferdinand. He attacks Mongo. Crawler Princess Donut puts herself between the blast and her dinosaur and lives only because of a cockroach ability, which is not a sentence I expected to generate this season. Some families skip the reunion. This one held it anyway, and it went about how you'd think.

beats.headline: The sir is part of his name
beats.text: Background from the caravan to the castle. Queen Imogen's familiar is Sir Ferdinand, rarely off her shoulder when not hunting away from the castle. The footman Theobold is firm that the title is not a title: a familiar, a pet, a lowly creature, the sir simply part of the name. Crawler Carl mentions that Ferdinand implied, out in the woods, that he was second in charge of the kingdom. You must be mistaken, says Theobold. Carl advises him to watch the cat.

beats.headline: On Carl's other shoulder
beats.text: A heavy weight lands on Carl's shoulder, the one Princess Donut is not standing on. Ferdinand, familiar of Queen Imogen, has come out of nowhere, and he repeats Florin's question back at Carl in a mocking voice: yeah, mate, you feeling okay? Carl's answer goes to Samantha, not to the cat. He's distracted, it says. Go, go, go.

beats.headline: The royal hat
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand, level 100 Province Boss, arrives in a gold turban with a white feather four feet high, and the crawlers around Carl laugh at him. It is his royal hat. It makes him the most handsome boy in the castle, and it carries a level-10 lightning spell. Charmed, he lets slip that the queen has him watching her sister and means to kill her once the party is over. Then he decides to visit Princess Donut in person, and bounds from the room.

beats.headline: I'll protect you, my bride
beats.text: The seal breaks, and Ferdinand, charmed to the whiskers, shouts up at the stage that he will protect his bride, and blinks out. When Imogen has Carl in the air with his bones snapping, the orange form of the cat slams into her head. She staggers and drops Carl, then backhands her own familiar across the room, the cat going one way and his hat the other. He hits the ground, yowls and disappears.

beats.headline: Ferdinand and his Bird
beats.text: Warlord Donut accepts Team Retribution's truce offer while her co-warlord is still in the middle of a sentence urging her to wait, and names the truce The Good Guys. Warlord Ferdinand of Team Retribution renames it Ferdinand and his Bird. The system does not let her change it back. The alliance itself stands: allied with the defenders, her crawlers will not be removed from Larracos when the ceasefire ends.

beats.headline: A bowler hat for Shanty Town
beats.text: Warlord on High, Sir Ferdinand, level 100, co-warlord of Team Retribution, arrives in the vestibule seated on his adjutant's head, in a turban improvised from tissues. He wants his rhinoceros mount and his hat. Carl offers a temporary replacement from Quan Ch's inventory, a bowler hat that decapitates and returns when thrown, in exchange for the mayorship of Shanty Town. The transfer requires Carl and Donut to pay gold. The trade is accepted, and the truce is renamed The Good Guys. Subject's remark on the matter: I'm a very handsome boy.

beats.headline: Five seconds of absolute chaos
beats.text: Warlord Ferdinand arrives at the production facility with five seconds of absolute chaos: don't hit me, I'm sorry, off the corner, across the room, off Carl's shoulder, circles, ears pinned. Then he sits up straight. How goes the war, kitten? No hat. He smells of smoke and alcohol and has not been grooming. A gnoll guard scans him while he hisses that he has his claws, you cur, and when the guards leave he tells them they are lucky they didn't get the slish slash. He wants to know where the snacks are.

beats.headline: An emergency action item
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand of Team Retribution proposed an emergency action item: gods who appear in Faction Wars do not have to go home right away. Juice Box told him to say a number of other things. He could not remember them. The request was split in two. The first half was denied; deity summoning rules stay as written. The second was approved: ascendency players must now pilot their sponsored deities when they are summoned, and may no longer appear as themselves. A pilot who had stayed back was corrected on the spot.

beats.headline: Kitten is in trouble
beats.text: Crawler Carl dived into a ditch in Shanty Town to get out of a defence tower's line of fire. Subject jumped in beside him, shaking, tail scorched from a near miss, bowler hat askew, and asked why he was lying down on the job, because Kitten is in trouble. Carl told him that going into the tower would get him killed and that Juice Box needs him alive. Subject reported that Juice Box hates him and is meaner than Bill. Carl told him that he, and Donut, want him alive too.

beats.headline: Anytime, babe
beats.text: Warlord Ferdinand turns up on Drick's bald head, wearing the bowler hat Princess Donut let him keep, to say yo before moseying down to the twelfth floor to bang some hot goddess chicks. He offers her a last-second fling. There are about four minutes, which he considers more than enough. She declines. Then she thanks him for trying to come save her in the tower. Anytime, babe. His transfer, with Juice Box's, is what defeats Team Retribution and hands the war to the Princess Posse.

beats.headline: Apartment 231, and a man named Bill
beats.text: The mandatory gate for Crawler Carl sits in apartment 231: a first-floor unit in his own building, not his own. On the couch, Marjory Williams and a friend, both with stitched eyes, discussing a man named Bill who keeps calling in breach of a restraining order. He drained her account, the friend says, broke her face, nearly killed her cat. The cat, large and orange, sleeps on top of the scratching tree the whole time. Here he is called Gravy Boat. Here, nobody wakes him.
